paras.en: When a solid solute dissolves in a solvent, it changes the vapour pressure[scan obscured] of the solvent. Similar effect is observed for a liquid solute in a liquid solvent[scan obscured] However, there is a major difference; a solid solute is usually non-volatile while[scan obscured] liquid solute is volatile. For example, if we analyse the vapour above a sugar[scan obscured] solution in water, we would find only water vapours, whereas, the vapours above[scan obscured] a solution of ethanol and water always contain both water and ethanol.

paras.en: The quantitative relationship between the vapour pressure of solution[scan obscured] composition of components of solution was given by F. M. Raoult. The Raoult[scan obscured] law states that the partial vapour pressure of any volatile component of[scan obscured] solution is equal to the vapour pressure of the pure component multiplied by[scan obscured] mole fraction of that component in solution. Those solutions which obey Raoult[scan obscured] law are called ideal solutions.

paras.en: Mathematically, Raoult's law can be written as P = P°X where P and P°[scan obscured] the partial vapour pressure of the component and that of the pure compo[scan obscured] respectively, and X is the mole fraction of the component in the solution.
